QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_32

question.text: Antyodaya Seva Sangh (rural development NPO) has an activity 'Conduct 100 agricultural training camps in drought-prone Marathwada villages'. Which of the following is MOST appropriately placed in the Assumptions column of the LFM?

answer.text: Training materials are printed and staff are deployed
Beneficiary farmers are willing to attend and local administration cooperates with venue permissions; monsoon conditions do not prevent access to villages
The sun rises in the east

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.2.11, assumptions are external factors or conditions that must hold for the project to succeed, beyond the direct control of the team — e.g., beneficiary willingness, local administrative cooperation, monsoon/weather conditions. Option B captures three such realistic externalities relevant to drought-zone training. The Trap: A describes inputs/internal readiness (SE-controlled). B, D are trivially true constants — listing them is padding, not risk management. Cross-Exam Context: Assumption-setting is tested in XXIII Ch 4/5/7 and parallels risk-assessment in SAS engagements and in statutory audit planning. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Good assumptions pass the 'what if this fails?' test. If the failure would materially alter outputs or outcomes, it belongs in the column. If not, it's noise.
